apc.d: vLLM feature that reuses already computed KV cache blocks when a new request starts with the same token prefix as an earlier one. Blocks are recognized by a chained hash; enabled with --enable-prefix-caching (the default in the V1 engine).

api-stateless.d: A contract in which the server doesn't keep the conversation between calls: the client resends the full history on every turn (as with /v1/chat/completions).

bloco-kv.d: A fixed-size page (block_size tokens) in which vLLM stores the KV cache. It is also the unit of hashing and reuse in prefix caching.

hash-encadeado.d: The key of a full block, computed from the previous block's hash, the block's token IDs and extra keys (cache_salt, LoRA, media). It identifies the entire prefix up to that point.

none-hash.d: Seed value used as the “parent hash” of the first block. Up to vLLM v0.29 it depended on the process's hash seed (PYTHONHASHSEED); since then it has been deterministic.

ref-count.d: The number of running requests that point to a block. A block with a ref_cnt greater than zero is never evicted; two requests can share the same physical block.

fila-livre.d: Doubly linked list of the blocks with ref_cnt = 0. Allocations take from the head; freed blocks return in reverse order and, upstream, all go to the tail (LRU). In the GLM recipe's image, according to its README, only hashed blocks go to the tail, while unhashed ones go to the front (LIFO).

lru.d: Eviction policy that removes the item used longest ago first.

evicao-preguicosa.d: A free block stays in the hash table — and can be reused — until someone needs its physical space; only then is the hash deleted.

taxa-de-acerto.d: The fraction of queried tokens that came from the cache: Δvllm:prefix_cache_hits ÷ Δvllm:prefix_cache_queries, measured as the difference of the counters before and after.

coordenador-hibrido.d: vLLM component (HybridKVCacheCoordinator) that combines the hits of each group: the final hit is the minimum across the participating groups, aligned to the LCM of the block sizes.

rascunhador.d: A small model or head that proposes tokens for the target model to verify in speculative decoding (MTP, EAGLE, DFlash2, DSpark). Many have their own KV or window.

eagle-block-drop.d: A conservative vLLM rule that discards the last matched prefix-cache block when there is an EAGLE-style drafter (MTP included); it can be turned off with disable_eagle_block_drop (vllm#53388).

replay-janela.d: Deliberately recomputing the last tokens of a cached prefix so that the drafter's sliding window is rebuilt (128 tokens in DSpark, 2,048 in GLM's DFlash2).

retencao-esparsa.d: Saving state or window checkpoints only every N tokens (the retention interval) instead of at every block: more history fits in the same pool, but late edits and branches recompute more.

cache-salt.d: A request field that enters as an extra key in the hash of the first block (and, through chaining, in all the following ones): requests with different salts don't share prefixes (namespaces), but they still write to the cache.

no-store.d: A per-request write opt-out (an overlay in the GLM recipe): the request reads the cache but inserts no hashes, and its blocks go back to the front of the free queue.

kv-connector.d: A vLLM plugin configured via --kv-transfer-config that moves KV blocks off the GPU or between instances (offload, persistence, disaggregated prefill).

lmcache.d: An off-GPU KV caching system (CPU RAM as L1 and disk as L2) that persists prefixes across restarts; used experimentally in the DeepSeek recipe.

estado-de-prompt-guardado.d: In TensorFold, a whole snapshot at a point of the prompt: the per-token rows stay in the conversation's extent, and the photo carries the KDA states, the convolution windows, the tail of the indexer rings and the DFlash2 window (and, at the end of the prompt, the logits row). A request whose prompt extends that point resumes from there with the same bits as a prefill from scratch. ~45 MiB fixed per entry in the GLM·TF recipe.

prefixo-compartilhado.d: Extra states that TensorFold keeps at the end of the system block (first <|user|>) and where the prompt stops matching a kept prompt: on the grid, ≥ 256 tokens past the resume point, at most 2 per request (SHARED_PREFIX=1). A new conversation with the same 7.9K-token system prompt starts in 0.13 s instead of 4.24 s.

replay-de-prompt.d: Full hit for an identical prompt: the state at the end of the prompt is kept along with the head's logits row, and the resend samples the first token from that row, with the same key, with no prefill at all. It only applies when the end falls on the 64-token grid. A 64K-token prompt: 34 s → under 0.07 s.

camada-de-spill.d: A disk floor for kept prompt states: states are written to local NVMe in 2,048-token blocks named by a chained hash, and read back instead of redoing the prefill. In the GLM·TF recipe, patches 0088 and 0128 (SPILL_GIB); in TensorFold's native engine, --spill-gib. A relative of LMCache and Dynamo's KV tiers.

espera-de-prefixo.d: When several requests arrive together with the same not-yet-kept prefix, only one prefills it; the others wait for its state and resume from there. In the GLM·TF recipe, PREFIX_WAIT=1 (six agents on a fresh 12-thousand-token system prompt: 47 → 15 s); in the native engine, TENSORFOLD_PREFIX_WAIT_MS.

estado-superado.d: A kept prompt state of a conversation that already has a longer state of its own (the next turn). In the GLM·TF recipe since v1.4 (patch 0063), it goes before the others when the state cap overflows; a shared prefix never counts as superseded (0077, 0120).
